About

Google Scholar, August 2026.

I apply and advance computer vision and AI methods — 3D reconstruction, depth estimation, image segmentation and image classification, together with large language models and multi-agent systems — in personalized nutrition and medical imaging.

I am completing my PhD at the AI in Health & Nutrition Lab, ARTORG Center, University of Bern, supervised by Prof. Stavroula Mougiakakou. My thesis is Multimodal AI-driven Personalized Nutrition.

Before the PhD I spent three years at SWIFT on Linux server administration and SAP GRC access control for production financial-messaging systems — which is why I care that research code runs in the field, not only that it publishes.

Research

Semi-automatic food segmentation

Prompt-based segmentation with a person in the loop: a click says what belongs to the item, the model returns the mask, and the annotation is then categorised and weighed. It cuts the cost of building food datasets without giving up mask quality.

3D vision: depth and reconstruction

A comparative study of sensor-, geometry- and neural-based methods for estimating food volume from images, evaluated against ground-truth volumes measured in 3D.

Robustness and the out-of-distribution problem

Fine-grained classification breaks the moment it meets a class it was never trained on. I benchmark post-hoc unknown-category detection so a model can abstain instead of guessing confidently.

Benchmarking post-hoc unknown-category detection

A worked setup: this classifier knows five dishes — dholl puri bol renversé rougaille pilaf gâteau piment. Everything else is out of distribution. Move the threshold τ: the model predicts a class when its score clears τ, and abstains when it does not. Can you find a τ with zero mistakes?

Multi-agent systems and knowledge graphs

Grounding language models on validated knowledge. The Swiss Food Knowledge Graph unites recipes, ingredients and their substitutions with nutrient data, allergen information, dietary restrictions and national nutrition guidelines, so a RAG pipeline can answer nutrition questions from verified facts rather than from what a model happens to have memorised.
